Honestly? It's tough. I have no idea what non-tech parents would do, but here's what my plans include:

  • A router with per-device config,
  • Logging so I can get a summary of most frequently hit sites, broken down by device. I don't have to look at it, just the knowledge that I might is enough. Also, this will get kids used to the idea that literally nothing you do on the Internet isn't viewable by somebody, which is an important thing to understand.
  • Until they are N years old, the router (and their devices as feasible) will have white lists so they have to ask to go somewhere first. A 7 year old shouldn't need very many websites beyond Wikipedia, Google with safe search, their school, and some other approved kid's sitesk as their interests dictate.
  • As time goes on, switch to a blacklist, there are many available that filter out a good amount of rubbish, and you can modify and add your own eg. Tumblr.
  • Eventually throw away the blacklist. But set up an alert if Tumblr and any fat acceptance sites are visited frequently!
  • Phones with data plans are tricker (no router to act as a choke point) but I'm sure it's do-able.

Now you can't stop everything (I used to go to my friends' house to watch the forbidden TV shows after all) but what it's about is reducing the frequency and scale of the exposure to nonsense, and clearly drawing the line that this here is acceptable for you now, and this over here is not.
